comments.text: The  Finns were forced into the Axis Powers during World War Two due to the Russian invasion of 1939. There is a story that prior to the invasion, the Finnish Premier visited Leningrad to meet with Stalin. Stalin talked at length while the Finnish Premier sat impassively listening. Stalin getting nowhere finally asked how many troops Finland had on the border. The Premier answered “Fifty thousand.” Stalin retorted “I have a hundred thousand ready to go. “ The Premier said nothing only taking notes. Stalin puzzled then queried what are you writing. The Premier replied “The orders to give each of my soldiers two bullets each.”

comments.text: The Grand Duchy arrangement is the detail that reframes the whole story — a century inside the Russian Empire while keeping its own currency and customs makes 'ruled' feel like the wrong word for most of that period. I'm curious how much of that autonomy was deliberate imperial policy, and how much was simply the cost of governing a distant, forested frontier.
